findings.evidence: Over about 5000 lines: read `--stat` first, give a high-level overview, and offer to deep-dive an area (for example "the API changes").
findings.fix: Turn the large-diff branch into a procedure. From the same-source `--stat`, cluster paths into candidate groups. findings.evidence: ## Gotchas — no item forbids state-changing git or gh commands while gathering the diff
findings.fix: Add: 'NEVER run `git checkout`, `git switch`, `gh pr checkout`, `git stash` or `git fetch` to inspect a source. Use `git show <rev>:<path>` and `gh pr diff` instead. Checking out a ref silently rewrites the user's worktree and can hide their uncommitted changes, which are the default thing this command explains.'

findings.evidence: Never group from a diff you did not see in full: page with `git diff --stat`, then read per-file diffs.
findings.fix: Line 66 contradicts line 38 ('never a bare `git diff --stat`'). Change it to: 'page with `--stat` on the same source as step 1 (for example `git diff --stat "<base>...<arg>"`, `git show --stat --format= "<arg>^{commit}"`, `gh pr diff "<pr>" --name-only`), then read per-file diffs with the same source and `-- <path>`.'

findings.evidence: compare the groups with the selected patch's file list (the manifest; if you use `--stat`, give it the same commit, range or branch comparison, never a bare `git diff --stat`)
findings.fix: Say how to build the manifest for every source, not only for git ranges. For the no-argument case, use `git diff HEAD --name-only` plus the `git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard` list, because untracked files are missing from `--stat`. For a PR, use `gh pr diff "<pr>" --name-only`. For `custom`, use the `diff --git` headers of the pasted patch.
